I disagree wholeheartedly. Both films stand on their own merits. The first film had a fresh start to do anything they wanted but they just rehashed the previous stories, laying the groundwork for the second to do the same. Then everything the second film switched up people hated. Both incredibly flawed movies. 

The first is great with the protagonist’s intro, the lightsaber fight, the droid, and some of the music, as well as the two main characters being likeable. 
Other than that, between the villain hideout of the superweapon, the really forced dialogue between the parents, the TV episode of the creature escape, the desert clone of the desert planet, the cantina 2.0, exclusive use of specific fighters, the awful meta commentary “This will begin to make things right” or “Aboard the Millennium Falcon with your father......Han......Solo.” etc as well as what I mentioned above with Mystery Boxes and Rebels vs Empire 2.0, the film was a severely lacking end product that capitalized on nostalgia and an audience starved for the franchise. 

The second is great with the bulk of the protagonist and mentor stuff as well as the protagonist and the antagonist (and the antagonist in general coming into his own), the companion’s sister, the mentor & the old master, the duel between the mentor and the antagonist (including- yes including the mentor’s Death), the villain’s death (good riddance) the Throne Room battle, Kamikaze Lightspeed, etc.  
Where it falls off the rails is the goat races, the absolute unnecessary inclusion of the companion and her god awful Love speech, the commander with purple hair, the pilot’s entire storyline, and the decision to make the rebels yet again smaller and smaller than even the first film where they were already too small (I mean seriously, it’s a fucking galaxy and they can’t find enough people to conquer a Keg Party), super destructible physics like the Bombers or the Big Not-Star Destroyer.

All in all, I find only a few scenes worth rewatching in the first film after multiple viewings, whereas I can watch more of the second without skipping around too much. That being said, the lows of the second are certainly much lower than the first, which was boring but safe. The second was either great or god awful. Regardless, both films stand on their own with their own weaknesses and strengths, but my long winded point is that the weaknesses of one don’t strengthen the other and vice versa.
